book.universe.probe_log.page.1:
UNV-7 SURVEY PROBE LOG

Main engine failure. Forced landing on this planet. Hull breached, primary systems offline.

To whoever finds this: the gear aboard can still be repaired.
book.universe.probe_log.page.2:
[MULTITOOL]
Damaged in the impact. Two copper ingots, two redstone and an iron ingot will fix it.

Hold USE: mining laser. It overheats if fired too long.
Sneak + USE: scan for nearby ore veins.
book.universe.probe_log.page.3:
[EXOSUIT]
Helmet and chestplate seal in your oxygen; the full set holds off cold, heat, toxins and radiation.

Oxygen capsules: bottled leaves.
Hazard cells: copper, redstone, coal.

Jetpack: jump again in mid-air.
book.universe.probe_log.page.4:
[SHIPS]
Build one from blocks: a helm, thrusters, fuel tanks; dress the hull as you like. Use the helm to assemble.

Fill the tanks with launch fuel (coal, gunpowder, a glass bottle).
Climb past the sky to reach space.
book.universe.probe_log.page.5:
[COURSE]
This planet has a moon: airless and cold, but rich in titanium.

In space the impulse engine gets you there fast. Fly into a body's atmosphere to land.

Better equipment needs titanium.
book.universe.probe_log.page.6:
[MISSION]
This probe belongs to the Universe Survey Programme.
All other probes have gone silent.

More worlds in this system await mapping.

— END OF LOG —

guide.universe.civilization.dialogue:
Aliens hang around stations, trading posts and settlements. Right-click to talk.

Once a day each:
Answer: pick what their race values
Gift: hold it in your main hand
Ask a word: once Acquainted

Right answer: +3 standing, a word and a reward. Traders pay credits, Scholars give data, Wardens give salvage. Sometimes a module.

Traders like valuables and food. Scholars like data and relics. Wardens like sentinel parts and weapons.
guide.universe.civilization.guilds:
Every mission belongs to a guild:
Delivery, mining: Merchants
Bounty, sentinels: Mercenaries
Survey, expeditions: Explorers

Done: +3 with the guild, +2 with the system's dominant race.

Station envoys offer two guild missions a day, better paid at higher ranks, and a gift for each new rank.

Ranks: Expelled, Novice, Member, Veteran, Elite, Master.
guide.universe.civilization.guilds.title: Guilds
guide.universe.civilization.language:
Each race has its own language of 64 words. You start out knowing eight: one, two, three, hydrogen, carbon, oxygen, star and light.

New words come from:
Knowledge stones: one each
Right answers: one from that speech
Gifts they like: one in return
Acquainted or better: ask each person for one a day

Known words show up translated when people talk. The Civilizations tab of the discovery log lists them.
guide.universe.civilization.merchant:
Every station and settlement has one. Talk to them and pick Browse Wares.

Three modules a day, mostly their race's specialty:
Traders: ship modules
Scholars: scanner and exosuit modules
Wardens: weapon and shield modules

Better standing, better stock: Regular and Friend get one grade up, Kindred two, with the last item A or better. Prices follow the station, minus your discount.

One of each per player per day.
guide.universe.civilization.races:
Three races share the cluster. Each system with a station is run by one of them, and most people you meet there belong to it. The star map and trade terminals show which.

Traders: profit
Scholars: knowledge
Wardens: valor

The home system belongs to the Traders.
guide.universe.civilization.races.title: Races
guide.universe.civilization.settlements:
Found on planets with an atmosphere that aren't barren. Scans mark them. The huts follow the system's dominant race: tents for Traders, white glass houses for Scholars, stone forts for Wardens.

A Knowledge Stone stands in the plaza
The stall's terminal works like a trading post's
Two visitors wait by the plaza
A tech merchant stands at the stall
guide.universe.civilization.standing:
Standing is kept per race and per guild, from -20 to 100, starting at 0.

Right answer +3, wrong answer -1
A gift they like: +2
Hitting one of them: -5

Hostile (< -5): won't talk, prices +10%
Stranger (-5)
Acquainted (10): ask for words
Regular (25): 5% off
Friend (45): 10% off
Kindred (70): 15% off

Prices follow the system's dominant race, at stations and trading posts alike.
guide.universe.civilization.stones:
Stone pillars carved with glowing script. Every planet you can land on has them, barren ones included, and scans mark them.

Right-click one to learn a word of the system's dominant race. Each stone teaches each player once; after that it just tells you you've read it.

They can't be mined or moved.
guide.universe.civilization.stones.title: Knowledge Stones
guide.universe.dark_fog.ammo:
Load ammo into the turret's ammo slot by hand, sorter or belt. One item fires several rounds.

Gauss: magnum, titanium and superalloy boxes, 40 rounds, each tier stronger.
Implosion: shell, high-explosive and crystal shell sets, 10 rounds.
Missile: missile, supersonic (faster) and gravity (pulls enemies together) sets, 8 rounds.
Craft magnum boxes by hand: copper, iron, copper in a row. The rest are easier in an assembler.
guide.universe.dark_fog.ammo.title: Ammo
guide.universe.dark_fog.attacks:
The more power your factory draws, the faster threat builds in bases on that planet. Hitting their buildings and units adds more.

At full threat a base sends raiders and rangers at the nearest, hungriest grid. You get a 30-second warning; they show up 80 blocks out, on the base's side. Guardians stay home.

Repel a wave and threat resets, then holds for 3 minutes. No attacks while nobody is on the planet.
guide.universe.dark_fog.attacks.title: Threat and Attacks
guide.universe.dark_fog.bases:
The Dark Fog builds bases on other planets, never your home world, 600–2000 blocks from the landing site: a core in the middle, a relay hovering above, camps and towers around. Bases level up when hit (0–30).

The relay powers the base; without it the base stalls once its stored energy runs out. Lost camps and towers return after 3 minutes. Within 64 blocks of you, camps overdrive and make units ten times faster.

Destroy the core and the base collapses into a core remnant. A geothermal station on it makes twice the power of lava.
guide.universe.dark_fog.bases.title: Dark Fog Bases
guide.universe.dark_fog.damage:
Only the Dark Fog can damage facilities; explosions can't. Look at a damaged facility to see its integrity bar.

At zero it breaks: its contents drop and a blue ghost stays behind. Right-click the ghost with the same block to put it back facing the same way. A logistics station keeps its cargo in the ghost.

With no blueprint work, construction drones repair nearby facilities and rebuild ghosts from blocks you carry.
guide.universe.dark_fog.damage.title: Damage and Ghosts
guide.universe.dark_fog.hive:
Systems with Dark Fog bases also have a hive in space, far out from the star: a core ringed by receivers, plasma towers, phase lasers and ports. Receivers turn starlight into matter, and each steals 3% of a Dyson sphere's power.

Power use slowly raises hive threat; hitting its relays raises it fast. At full threat, lancers bomb the planet you are on (never home). The hive also sends relays to found bases, and later seeds.

Kill the core and the hive collapses, but it rebuilds in 10 minutes while a relay remains in the system.
guide.universe.dark_fog.hive.title: Space Hives
guide.universe.dark_fog.lancers:
A hive at full threat sends lancers to bomb the planet you are on. You get 20 seconds' warning, and the HUD marks where they will appear.

They drop to about 28 blocks up, or stop just above a shield dome, and bomb the facilities below, 8 bombs each. Blasts damage facilities within about 3 blocks.

Shields soak up the bombs. Only missile and plasma turrets reach lancers at altitude. Out of bombs, or down to one or two, they climb away. Humpbacks stay home to guard the hive.
guide.universe.dark_fog.lancers.title: Lancer Raids
guide.universe.dark_fog.loot:
Dark Fog drops sand and parts, better ones at higher levels: energy shards (0+), neurons and Dark Fog matrices (3+), recombinators (6+), singularities (12+), core elements (18+). Drops vanish after 2 minutes.

The Dark Fog matrix is the seventh matrix. Research Dark Fog Analysis first.

Parts swap for intermediates: recombinators make graphene, shards make plasma exciters, neurons make processors.
guide.universe.dark_fog.loot.title: Drops and Dark Fog Matrices
guide.universe.dark_fog.plasma:
Plasma turret: range 56, takes plasma or antimatter capsules. Fast plasma bolts burst on impact. Hits ground, air and high altitude, out to 96 for high targets.

SR plasma turret: range 16, power only, heavy hits, no high altitude. High idle draw.

Lancers bomb from high altitude. Only missile and plasma turrets reach them.

The Hives tab on the fleet terminal sends frigates to strike a hive. They bring back Dark Fog loot.
guide.universe.dark_fog.plasma.title: Plasma Turrets
guide.universe.dark_fog.relays:
Every so often the hive sends out a relay. It flies through space for 45 seconds, where you can shoot it, spends three to five minutes in transit, then drops out of the sky. Missile and plasma turrets can hit it during that 30-second descent.

Relays head for the planet in the system that uses the most power (never home) and land a few hundred blocks from your facilities, founding a new base. A base that lost its relay is resupplied first.

Relays won't land under a shield. They wait in orbit for two minutes and try again, and give up after five tries.
guide.universe.dark_fog.relays.title: Relays
guide.universe.dark_fog.repair:
Needs power. Repairs facilities within 30 blocks, rebuilds ghosts from blocks in its storage and picks up items within 45.

Set it to take only Dark Fog drops or only what it already stores. Sorters can load and unload it. It is tough enough to use as a wall.
guide.universe.dark_fog.repair.title: Battlefield Analysis Base
guide.universe.dark_fog.seeds:
At level 8 the hive releases seeds. A seed flies to the nearest system within 15 light years that has no hive, taking ten minutes to an hour, and grows a new hive there.

The star map shows its route and where it is now. You can shoot it during the first and last minute of the trip.

Relays and seeds drop Dark Fog materials. Shoot one down from a ship in space and the loot goes straight into the hold.
guide.universe.dark_fog.seeds.title: Seeds
guide.universe.dark_fog.shield:
Charging takes 24 kW. At 1.44 MJ the dome rises over 32 blocks; at 2.88 MJ it spans 160, 64 high. Upkeep is 12 kW.

It stops damage from above at 1 kJ per point and drops when empty. Relays can't land under it; ground units walk through. Up to 80 work per planet; where domes overlap, the fuller one takes the hit.
guide.universe.dark_fog.shield.title: Planetary Shields
guide.universe.dark_fog.support:
Signal tower: power pole, range 12, links within 30. Powered, it draws Dark Fog within 48 blocks and lends its range to missile turrets on its grid. Near a Dark Fog base it overdrives the camps.

Jammer tower: slows Dark Fog within 16 blocks to 70% speed; with capsules, 24 blocks and 40% (10 s per capsule).

Throwables: right-click to throw. They burst on impact without breaking blocks: 6 (+fire), 16, 32 damage.
guide.universe.dark_fog.support.title: Towers and Throwables
guide.universe.dark_fog.turrets:
Turrets need power and pick targets in range on their own, Dark Fog attacking facilities first. Low power means slow fire.

Gauss: range 32, 6 shots/s, ammo boxes, less accurate far out. Available first.
Laser: range 24, no ammo, weak but never misses, power-hungry.
Implosion cannon: range 40, ground only, arcing shells, area damage.
Missile: range 48, homing, area damage and knockback. Also hits targets near a signal tower on its grid.
Gauss and laser turrets need line of sight.
guide.universe.dark_fog.turrets.title: Turrets
guide.universe.dark_fog.world_options:
Create World > More > Game Rules, under Universe. In an existing world use /gamerule.

Dark Fog: on/off, aggressiveness, initial level, occupation, growth
Threat factors: power use, combat
Sentinel strength: 0 means no sentinels
Resource multiplier: 0 means infinite
Star systems: 32 to 256

The star system count is fixed once the world exists. The rest can change any time.
guide.universe.dyson.design:
Once a layer has a template, click Edit in the editor to change it yourself:
Node — click to place one; it snaps to the lat/long grid, hold Shift for a finer snap
Frame — click two nodes to connect them, and keep clicking to keep going
Shell — click inside a loop of frames, or press Fill to cover every loop at once
Erase — delete what you click

Nodes and frames that are already built cannot be deleted directly: select them and press Demolish first. Structure points are not refunded.

Nodes, frames and shells can be coloured: pick a colour and use the paint tool, or select a batch and press Paint. That is the colour you see in the sky and in space.

Copy exports the layer as a string, saves it to your library and puts it on the clipboard, so you can paste it into chat or online. Import takes someone else's string, and only works on a layer with nothing built.
guide.universe.dyson.design.title: Designing a Shell
guide.universe.dyson.editor:
Press Y for the Dyson sphere editor, or open it from an ejector, silo or receiver.

Swarm: up to 20 orbits
Shell: up to 10 layers; pick a grid (geodesic, honeycomb, lat-long), build nodes and frames, then shells
Latitude: within 30 degrees at first; Dyson Stress I and II raise it to 60 and 90
Material: each built node pulls 10 sails a minute from the swarm
guide.universe.dyson.editor.title: Dyson Sphere Editor
guide.universe.dyson.receiver:
Ray receivers bring the sphere's power down. Full efficiency after 20 min of steady reception; 2 min off resets it.

Power mode: 6 to 15 kW
Photon mode: critical photons, 6/min max
Graviton lens: doubles power, one per 10 min
guide.universe.dyson.receiver.title: Ray Receiver
guide.universe.dyson.rockets:
Nodes and frames are built with rockets from a vertical launching silo.

Rate: one rocket every 12 s
Needs: open sky
Power: 18 kW
Rocket: lands in 20 s, +1 structure point
Per structure point: 96 W
guide.universe.dyson.rockets.title: Rockets
guide.universe.dyson.sails:
The EM-Rail Ejector fires solar sails into the swarm; pick the orbit in its screen.

Rate: one sail every 3 s
Needs: star 5° above horizon, or in space
Lifetime: 90 min
Per sail: 36 W x star luminosity factor
guide.universe.dyson.sails.title: Solar Sails
guide.universe.endgame.advanced:
Green matrices unlock four advanced machines. They run the same recipes as the machines below them, only faster.

Negentropy Smelter: speed 3, 2.88 kW
Re-composing Assembler: speed 3, 2.7 kW
Quantum Chemical Plant: speed 2, 2.16 kW
Self-evolution Lab: 3x research, 1.92 kW
guide.universe.endgame.advanced.title: Advanced Machines
guide.universe.endgame.antimatter:
The miniature particle collider turns critical photons into antimatter.

Power: 12 kW
Research: Dirac Inversion Mechanism

Antimatter goes into universe matrices and fuel rods. 12 antimatter, 12 hydrogen, a constraint sphere and a titanium alloy make 2 rods.
guide.universe.endgame.antimatter.title: Antimatter
guide.universe.endgame.finale:
Mission Complete is the last tech: 3,000 points of white matrices only.
Finishing it plays the ending. The game carries on afterwards and upgrades stay open.
Replay the ending from the Ending chapter.
guide.universe.endgame.finale.title: Mission Complete
guide.universe.endgame.power:
Mini Fusion Power Plant
15 kW from deuteron fuel rods, 6 min per rod at full load

Artificial Star
72 kW from antimatter fuel rods, 15 min per rod at full load
guide.universe.endgame.power.title: Fusion and Artificial Stars
guide.universe.endgame.white:
Universe matrices (white) fund Mission Complete and the four uncapped upgrade lines.

Universe matrix: composite + information + gravity + antimatter
Composite matrix: blue + red + yellow
guide.universe.endgame.white.title: Universe Matrix
guide.universe.ending.done: Press the button below to replay the ending and this world's statistics.
guide.universe.ending.locked: Finish Mission Complete to replay the ending here.
guide.universe.exploration.bases:
Place a base beacon to register a base; right-click to rename. No research.

Teleporters reach your bases and stations you've visited.
Cost: 12 kJ per jump, 10 s to recharge
Range: stand within 6 blocks
Pets within 24 blocks come along
Research: Teleport Network
guide.universe.exploration.bases.title: Bases and Teleporters
guide.universe.exploration.discoveries:
Press K for the discovery log. Systems are logged when you enter space, planets when you land.
Discoverers can rename them, up to 24 characters.

New system: 5 to 20 survey data (black holes the most)
New planet: 3 or 4

Survey data goes into hand-in research (Interstellar Survey, Technology Modules, Warp Calibration) and grade C modules, and it sells.
guide.universe.exploration.exotic:
Every exotic world has one landform you can see all over it, one of six, each taken from a real place on Earth or Mars.

Columnar basalt: fields of six-sided columns stepping down into shallow water, with the odd lone tower
Hoodoos: thin crowded rock spires, each under a hard caprock
Giant crystals: shafts tens of blocks long slanting out of the ground in clusters, in water too
Concretions: round boulders half buried in the ground, the big ones cracked with white veins, small dark spherules scattered around
Polygonal ground: a net of polygons on the flats with low ridges along the edges — ice wedges where it is cold, salt crust where it is hot and dry, sorted stones otherwise
Arches: sandstone fins, some pierced through into an arch

The star map, discovery log and analysis visor all name which one. The terrain keeps clear of landing sites, portals, sentinel pillars, points of interest and landmarks.
guide.universe.exploration.exotic.title: Exotic Terrain
guide.universe.exploration.facility:
Only on planets with sentinels. The walls can't be broken; the reinforced door is the only way in.

Reinforced Door: cut it with the multitool in mining mode for 10 seconds. Pausing to cool down is fine, but leave it too long and you start over. Opening it puts you at wanted level 3
Facility Terminal: pick one of three tech modules, once per player
Two drones and a quad come to patrol outside when someone approaches
guide.universe.exploration.fossils:
Habitable, barren, scorched and frozen planets have abandoned fossil digs. Multitool scans mark them.

The pit floor shows 6–10 Fossil Dirt. Dig each with a shovel for one fossil:
Coiled Shell Fossil: common
Arthropod Fossil: uncommon
Skull Fossil: rare, worth the most

Fossils are sell-only.
guide.universe.exploration.fossils.title: Fossil Pits
guide.universe.exploration.fulgurite:
In thunderstorms, lightning that hits sand, soil or rock sometimes fuses a glass tube down into the ground: fulgurite. Mine it with a pickaxe and sell it at a station.

Rainy planets get thunderstorms, and volcanic ash storms throw lightning too. Strikes near bases and buildings leave none.

Lightning can hit you. Don't stand in the open during a storm.
guide.universe.exploration.giants:
Some habitable, exotic and ocean worlds have a giant species, 3.5 to 6 blocks tall. Giants roam alone on open ground.

The ground shakes within 24 blocks as they walk
Health 120 to 200, slow
Docile ones flee when hit; territorial ones stomp back
First scan: 5 survey data

Tame and ride one like any other creature. It steps up one-block ledges but barely jumps.
guide.universe.exploration.giants.title: Giants
guide.universe.exploration.observatory:
The Observatory Terminal finds the nearest place you haven't been within 3,000 blocks and marks it on your HUD: Precursor Ruins, a portal you haven't reached, or a Sentinel Pillar.

Each observatory works once per player. If it finds nothing in range, the use doesn't count.
guide.universe.exploration.pillars:
Every planet with sentinels has one Sentinel Pillar, 400–900 blocks from the landing site: a tall tower with amber light strips.

Base terminal: right-click to shut down this planet's sentinels for 20 minutes
Once per in-game day
No response while you are wanted
Right-click with a Walker Brain: trade it for a Sentinel multitool, once per pillar

Clear the level 5 wave and the pillar is marked on your HUD.
guide.universe.exploration.pillars.title: Sentinel Pillars
guide.universe.exploration.poi:
Scans mark nearby points of interest.

Drop pod: repair to expand your exosuit
Monolith: 3 survey data and a portal glyph the first time
Tech cache: break it for a module
Signal booster: finds one within 2,000 blocks
guide.universe.exploration.poi.title: Points of Interest
guide.universe.exploration.portals:
Every landable planet has a Precursor portal carved with its address: 6 glyphs out of 16. Your ship can't follow you through.

Learning glyphs: each monolith's first touch and each portal's first visit teach one; exploration expeditions may bring one back
Dialing: right-click the dial and enter 6 known glyphs; the portal opens for 30 s, walk into the light
The star map shows the address of planets you've visited
guide.universe.exploration.portals.title: Precursor Portals
guide.universe.exploration.salvage:
Salvage sites: scorched ground and a lit beacon. Dig down through 3 shell plates at the center to the salvage capsule, then right-click it once to spill salvaged scrap and parts. Scrap is sell-only.

Abandoned buildings: old habitat modules with broken doors. The data terminal gives navigation data the first time you read it, and there's a supply crate.
guide.universe.exploration.salvage.title: Salvage and Abandoned Buildings
guide.universe.exploration.submarine:
Water only. Deploy it on the water; three pickaxe hits pack it up with fuel and cargo.

W / S: thrust, A / D: strafe
Look up to rise, down to dive
Hold left-click: torpedo, 4 fuel each
Sonar: multitool right-click, 600 blocks
The cabin has air and no pressure
Tank 1,000 (ship fuel), hold 18 slots
guide.universe.exploration.trading_post:
Planets with an atmosphere that aren't barren have trading posts. Multitool scans mark them. Ships can land on any of the three landing pads.

Trading Post Terminal: shares the system station's market and prices, with fewer goods. Launch fuel, oxygen, hazard cells and space warpers are always in stock; only one tech module
Two supply crates inside

Trades here move the station's prices too.
guide.universe.exploration.underwater:
Seas hide a lot on the seabed.

Candlelight Kelp: glows when ripe; stay close to refill oxygen. A Kelp Sac restores 15 oxygen and can be replanted
Clams: on deep seabeds. Right-click one for a Living Pearl, which sells high
Fish school, eels bite swimmers, jellyfish sting, giant squid keep to deep water

Pressure: deeper than 40 blocks below sea level, the exosuit uses oxygen 50% faster.
guide.universe.exploration.visor:
The analysis visor identifies creatures, plants, ores, stars and planets. Hold the multitool, press V, aim and hold right-click for 1.2 s.
On creatures it also shows diet, produce and whether you can ride them.

First discoverer gets survey data:
Creature: 2
Plant, tree, mineral: 1
Whole planet's wildlife: +5
guide.universe.exploration.visor.title: Analysis Visor
guide.universe.exploration.wrecks:
Deep seabeds hide shipwrecks and seabed ruins. Submarine sonar and multitool scans both find them.

Shipwrecks: the cargo crates hold salvaged parts
Seabed ruins: half buried, with 3 sealed crates inside

Sealed crates are worth more than the supply crates on land.
guide.universe.exploration.wrecks.title: Wrecks and Ruins
guide.universe.gathering.fluids:
Oil Extractor
Two blocks tall, lower half on a crude oil seep. 0.5 to 1.5 crude oil per second, slowing as it drains, down to 30%. Power 840 W.

Water Pump
Sits on a water source. 50 water a minute for 300 W. On an acid source it pumps sulfuric acid at the same rate.
guide.universe.gathering.fluids.title: Oil and Water
guide.universe.gathering.mining:
The mining machine mines ore below it and outputs from its front. With several ores in range it mines only the most common one.

Area: 5x5, 3 layers deep
Rate: 1 item per ore block every 40 s
Power: 420 W
Research: Electromagnetism
guide.universe.gathering.mining.title: Mining Machine
guide.universe.gathering.smelting:
The arc smelter smelts with electricity and has three input slots: ingots, steel, graphite, silicon, titanium and glass.
Sorters feeding it only insert what the recipe needs.

Power: 360 W
Raw ore to ingot: 1 s
3 iron ingots to steel: 3 s (Steel Smelting)
guide.universe.gathering.smelting.title: Arc Smelter
guide.universe.gathering.veins:
Each ore block holds a set amount and turns back into stone when empty.

Reserve: 400 to 1200, times planet abundance 0.5 to 1.5
Overworld: surface outcrops of iron, copper and coal, some gold and crude oil seeps
Other planets: titanium, silicon, sulfur, fire ice, optical crystal, uranium and more, by planet type

A multitool scan finds veins fastest.
guide.universe.gathering.veins.title: Ore Veins
guide.universe.husbandry.companions:
Tamed creatures become companions. Sneak + right-click one empty-handed to open its screen.

Trust: 50 when tamed, +5 a meal, up to +10 a day
Fed: lasts two days; a meal fills half. Hunger costs trust
Mood: happy when fed and trust is 70+
Dig: once a day for ore, survey data or a rare tech module. Happy ones find more
Eggs: one every two days if over half fed and trust is 50+
guide.universe.husbandry.eggs:
Well-fed companions that trust you lay an egg now and then.

Place it on a solid block. It cracks twice and hatches in 5 minutes
The hatchling is a companion of the mother's owner
A ready egg waits until its owner is online
Mining it gives it back, progress lost

The egg carries species, size, color and temperament, and the hatchling takes after it.
guide.universe.husbandry.eggs.title: Creature Eggs
guide.universe.husbandry.exocraft:
A drivable mining vehicle. Use it on the ground to deploy; three pickaxe hits pack it up with its fuel and cargo.

Right-click to get in, sneak to get out
W / S: throttle, A / D: steer
Hold left-click: mining laser, 12 blocks
Vein scan: multitool right-click, 64 blocks

Tank: 1,000 (ship fuel), hold: 27 slots
guide.universe.husbandry.exocraft.title: Exocraft
guide.universe.husbandry.produce:
Tamed creatures produce items, follow you, and the big ones can be ridden.

Produce: drops 30 s after a meal, once every 5 min
Follow: from 10 blocks, teleports past 12
Sneak + empty hand: companion screen (next page)
Riding: large quadrupeds, hexapods and bipeds; right-click with an empty hand, hold jump to charge
guide.universe.husbandry.produce.title: Produce and Riding
guide.universe.husbandry.sequencer:
Egg in the top slot, material below. Each change takes 5 s; nothing is used up if there's nothing to change.

Bio gel: size +0.1 (up to ×1.5)
Bone meal: size -0.1 (down to ×0.5)
Dye: that color
Herbivore feed: docile
Raw meat: territorial
guide.universe.husbandry.sequencer.title: Egg Sequencer
guide.universe.husbandry.summoner:
Right-click to list your deployed vehicles, then pick one to call it to the front of the pad.

Same dimension: moved straight over
Other dimensions: packed up and rebuilt here, fuel and cargo kept
Submarines need water in front
Vehicles in your inventory aren't listed
A vehicle belongs to whoever deploys it.
guide.universe.husbandry.summoner.title: Vehicle Summoner
guide.universe.husbandry.taming:
The visor shows what a creature eats. Feed it once a second; each bite may tame it.

Herbivores: wheat, carrots, apples, feed
Carnivores: raw meat, carnivore feed
Chance: docile 35%, skittish 25%, territorial 15%, predator 8%
guide.universe.husbandry.taming.title: Taming
guide.universe.husbandry.vehicles:
They deploy, pack up and refuel like the exocraft.

Hover car: fastest. Floats a block up and crosses water. 18-slot hold
Heavy rover: slow, eight wheels, 54-slot hold. Sneak + right-click the rear for its portable refiner, which works on the move
Exo mech: slow, steps up 2 blocks. Hold jump for up to 3 s of jets; land to recharge. Sealed cabin with air. Left-click: blaster cannon. 27-slot hold
guide.universe.husbandry.vehicles.title: More Vehicles
guide.universe.logistics.assembler:
Assemblers craft the recipe picked in their screen. Each slot takes only its own ingredient, and automation fills up to 4 crafts.

Mk.I: speed 0.75, 260 W
Mk.II: speed 1.0, 540 W
Mk.III: speed 1.5, 1.08 kW
guide.universe.logistics.assembler.title: Assemblers
guide.universe.logistics.belts:
Belts carry items the way you faced when placing them. Mobs and dropped items ride along.

Sneak + empty hand: flat, up, down
Empty hand: take items off
Speed: 6, 12 or 30 items/s by tier
guide.universe.logistics.belts.title: Conveyor Belts
guide.universe.logistics.blueprint:
Blueprints copy builds with recipes and filters, splitter priority and filter, traffic monitor thresholds, matrix lab proliferator mode and battlefield base pickup. Priority outputs turn with the blueprint.

Blank: mark two corners (32 max per side), sneak + right-click to save
Saved: right-click to place, R rotates, sneak + right-click clears
Range: 64 blocks
Survival: your drones build it
Creative: placed at once
guide.universe.logistics.blueprint.title: Blueprints
guide.universe.logistics.distributor:
Sits on a chest or depot and handles one item. Bots supply and collect for nearby mechas and other distributors.

Range: 64 blocks
Bots: 10 max, 8 items a trip at 6 m/s
Battery: 60 kJ, 20 J per block flown
Research: Distribution Logistics
guide.universe.logistics.drones:
In survival a blueprint places a blue site. Your mecha's drones build it from the bottom up, nearest first, using materials from inventory and cargo. Placing the right block yourself counts too.

Range: 64 blocks
Drones: 3 at 6 m/s, 4 blocks a trip; more and faster with Communication Control and Drone Engine
Blueprint size: 300 blocks, more with Mass Construction
The HUD shows what is missing; the mecha panel can clear sites
guide.universe.logistics.drones.title: Construction Drones
guide.universe.logistics.piling:
The automatic piler stacks matching cargo so one belt slot carries several. It waits up to 1 s for a full pile. The pile sorter moves whole piles, 12 a second.
Pile size comes from the Cargo Stacking upgrade: 2 at first, up to 4.

The traffic monitor counts items over the last minute. Right-click to set an alarm floor, or right-click with an item to count only that. Below the floor it lights red and emits redstone; it starts checking after a minute.

Research: Integrated Logistics, Pile Sorting
guide.universe.logistics.piling.title: Piling
guide.universe.logistics.proliferator:
Spray coaters sit in a belt line and spray passing cargo. Right-click with a proliferator to load, empty-handed to check.
Machines fed sprayed ingredients offer extra products or speedup in their screen, at a power cost. Mixed batches count the lowest level.

Points, sprays, extra / speed, power:
Mk.I: 1, 12, +12.5% / +25%, +30%
Mk.II: 2, 24, +20% / +50%, +70%
Mk.III: 4, 60, +25% / +100%, +150%
Sprayed fuel burns longer; sprayed matrices give extra research.
guide.universe.logistics.slots:
The 12 slots on the right of the mecha panel each hold an item with a min and max. Below the min (inventory plus cargo), a supplying distributor sends bots; above the max, a collecting one takes the surplus, plain items only.

Limits: 0-9999
Mecha modes: off, supply, collect, both
Between distributors: demand fetches from supply
guide.universe.logistics.slots.title: Logistics Slots
guide.universe.logistics.sorters:
Sorters move items from the block behind to the block in front, only what fits.

Right-click with item: set filter
Empty hand: clear filter
Speed: 1.5, 3 or 6 moves/s
Splitters alternate between outputs. Storage Mk.I has 30 slots.
guide.universe.logistics.sorters.title: Sorters
guide.universe.logistics.splitter:
Right-click a side of a splitter empty-handed to make it the priority output; click again to clear. Cargo takes the priority side first and spills to the others when it backs up.
With a priority set, right-click with an item to filter: that item goes only to the priority side, everything else to the rest. Sneak + empty hand clears the filter.

Storage depots stack. Belt input fills upward, and a sorter on the bottom depot reaches the whole stack.
guide.universe.logistics.splitter.title: Splitters and Stacked Storage
guide.universe.logistics.stations:
Stations send and receive by each slot's settings. Drones serve one dimension; vessels travel between planets.
Set each slot's item and limit, then storage, supply or demand for local and remote. Stations charge only from grid surplus.

Planetary: 4 slots x 5,000, drone range 1,000 by default
Interstellar: 5 slots x 10,000 plus vessels; other systems cost 2 space warpers a trip
guide.universe.logistics.stations.title: Logistics Stations
guide.universe.logistics.vessels:
Vessels from interstellar stations are visible in system space: they rise out of the departure planet's atmosphere, cross to the destination and dive in.
Trips to other systems warp out at the system edge, stretching as they go. Routes curve around the star.
guide.universe.logistics.vessels.title: Vessels in Space
guide.universe.power.exchanger:
The exchanger charges accumulator items, or drains full ones back into the grid, so you can carry power to a site with no generators.
Switch modes in its screen. Accumulators that don't match the mode go straight to the output.

Rate: 45 kW
One accumulator: 4 s
Research: Energy Exchanger
guide.universe.power.exchanger.title: Energy Exchanger
guide.universe.power.generators:
Wind Turbine
300 W x wind factor. Higher is windier; rain x1.2, thunder x1.5. Nothing on airless planets.

Solar Panel
360 W with open sky, scaled by sun height and star brightness. Zero at night. Faces the star in space.

Thermal Power Plant
Up to 2.16 kW from vanilla fuel, burning only what the grid draws. Coal lasts 11 s at full load.
guide.universe.power.generators.title: Generators
guide.universe.power.geothermal:
Place it over lava; the block directly below must be lava. No fuel, and it only produces what the grid draws.

Max: 4.8 kW
Scorched planets and the Nether: 7.2 kW
Research: Geothermal Extraction
guide.universe.power.geothermal.title: Geothermal Power
guide.universe.power.grid:
Tesla towers power nearby devices and link to each other into a grid. No wires.
When power runs short, accumulators discharge first, then all machines slow down evenly.

Power radius: 6 blocks
Link distance: 12 blocks
Right-click a tower to see its numbers. The stats screen (O) has a power panel.
guide.universe.power.grid.title: The Grid
guide.universe.power.interface:
Place it inside a tower's range. Every face takes cables and devices from other mods; 1 J counts as 1 FE.
Input: feeds incoming power into the grid
Output: pushes grid power into adjacent devices

Rate: up to 45 kW
Research: Grid Interface

Storage tanks, water pumps and oil extractors also take pipes from other mods. One fluid item is 1000 mB.
guide.universe.power.interface.title: Power from Other Mods
guide.universe.power.storage:
Accumulators charge from surplus and discharge when generation falls short. They keep their charge when broken.

Capacity: 180 kJ
Rate: up to 2.7 kW
Research: Energy Storage
guide.universe.power.storage.title: Accumulators
guide.universe.power.towers:
All three towers join the same grid; only their reach differs.

Tesla tower: power 6, link 12
Wireless power tower: power 4, link 10. Refills oxygen and hazard protection for exosuits within 5 blocks, drawing 1.5 kW while charging
Satellite substation: power 20, link 40

Research: Wireless Power, Satellite Power Distribution
guide.universe.power.towers.title: Power Towers
guide.universe.research.hand_in:
Press J for the tech tree. Early techs take a hand-in instead of a lab. Research is shared server-wide.

Electromagnetism: 10 coils, 10 boards. Tesla tower, wind turbine, mining machine
Automatic Metallurgy: 20 iron, 10 coils. Arc smelter
Basic Assembling: 20 boards, 20 gears. Assembler
Electromagnetic Matrix: 10 boards, 10 coils. Matrix lab
guide.universe.research.hand_in.title: Hand-in Research
guide.universe.research.lab:
Matrix labs turn matrices into research points. Pick a current research in the tech tree; every 5 s a lab uses one of each required matrix for one point. Labs add up.

Power: 480 W
Automation: up to 10 per slot
Research: Electromagnetic Matrix
guide.universe.research.lab.title: Matrix Lab
guide.universe.research.matrices:
All six matrices are made in assemblers; later techs need more colors.

Blue: coil + circuit board
Red: 2 energetic graphite + 2 hydrogen
Yellow: diamond + titanium crystal
Purple: 2 processors + particle broadband
Green: graviton lens + quantum chip, makes 2
White: composite + purple + green + antimatter
guide.universe.research.matrices.title: The Six Matrices
guide.universe.research.stacking:
Labs stack. Each second a lab takes matrices from the one below until both hold the same, so feed only the bottom one. Sprayed points carry over.

Self-evolution Lab: 3x speed, 1.92 kW, stacks with matrix labs
Research: Self-evolution Research
guide.universe.research.stacking.title: Stacking Labs
guide.universe.research.upgrades:
The rightmost column of the tech tree holds the upgrades. Early levels use lower matrices; research continues by itself while the next level needs the same ones.

Vein Utilization: mining +10%, drain x0.94
Research Speed: +25%
Carrier Engine: +25%
Ray Transmission: loss x0.85
Carrier Capacity: +10%
Solar Sail Life: +15 min
(all per level)

The first four end in white-matrix levels with no cap; capacity and sail life have 6 levels each.
guide.universe.research.upgrades.title: Upgrades
guide.universe.ship.black_hole:
One system in six has a black hole, 30,000 to 45,000 blocks from the star. It's in the autopilot list and on the space HUD.

Fly within 150 blocks of the horizon: no warper, no drive tier, and you're thrown to a far-off system
Cost: 30% hull, shields emptied

The star map marks systems with a black hole.
guide.universe.ship.black_hole.title: Black Holes
guide.universe.ship.build:
Ships are built from blocks. Right-click the helm to assemble everything connected to it; terrain is left out.

Required: one helm (its facing is the bow), at least one thruster
Optional: fuel tanks, impulse engines, warp drives, shields, weapons, seats, hull plating
Limit: 4,096 blocks
Lift-off: thrust-to-weight above 1; one thruster lifts 12 t at 1 g
guide.universe.ship.build.title: Building a Ship
guide.universe.ship.cargo:
Chests and barrels on your ship are its cargo. Sit in the ship and press the cargo key: every hold on board shows up in one screen, in flight too.

Mined asteroids and pirate wrecks drop straight into cargo. The more it is worth, the more pirates want it.
guide.universe.ship.cargo.title: Cargo
guide.universe.ship.dealer:
Each station hangar has a ship dealer with 4 ships a day, priced by blocks and grade. Bought ships wait fueled on the pad. Ships you park in the hangar sell for 60%.

Summon (N): call your main ship on the ground or in a station; it lands on a pad within 64 blocks
Autopilot (N in space): pick a planet, station, freighter or signal; steer to cancel
Landing pad: powered; refuels ships up to 4 blocks above it
Crashed ships: right-click the damaged helm with 4 titanium ingots and 2 circuit boards
guide.universe.ship.dealer.title: Buying and Summoning
guide.universe.ship.drives:
Some stars are out of reach with a plain warp drive. Fit a drive in a tech slot; the star map says which one. Each drive also covers the tiers below it.

Warp drive: M, K, G, F stars
Cadmium drive: red giants
Emeril drive: A-type white stars, white dwarfs
Indium drive: B and O blue stars, neutron stars, black holes

Research a drive, then make it in an assembler.
guide.universe.ship.drives.title: Drive Tiers
guide.universe.ship.encounters:
Piloting more than 600 blocks from a station, you may pick up a signal every 6 to 10 minutes. It's marked on the HUD and listed as Signal in the autopilot.

Derelict freighter: fly into the hangar and search the crates; the captain's safe is at the front. No gravity or air inside. Keep out from under sparking conduits. Gone after 30 min
Distress call: clear the pirates within 3 min. No freighter yet? The captain gives you this one; otherwise 15,000 credits. Don't hit the freighter
guide.universe.ship.encounters.title: Space Encounters
guide.universe.ship.fleet:
With a freighter you can hire frigates at a ship dealer, up to 12. The fleet terminal offers 3 expeditions a day.

Types: combat, exploration, industry, trade, support
Expeditions: 1–5 stars, 10–40 min, up to 5 frigates, paid in launch fuel
Each leg checks the team's stat; a failure damages a frigate, a second one sinks it
Rewards: credits, materials, modules, sometimes a portal glyph

Frigates level up every 4 expeditions.
guide.universe.ship.fleet.title: Frigates and Expeditions
guide.universe.ship.fly:
Right-click a fuel tank with fuel, then assemble at the helm; you start in the pilot seat.

WASD: thrust and turn
Space / Sneak: up / down
Sprint: impulse engine (space only)
Left-click: fire, G: switch weapon
Hold Sneak 1 s after landing: park as blocks

To space: 48 blocks above the world's top
To land: fly into a planet's atmosphere
Fuel: coal 200, coal block 1,800, launch fuel 1,000
The cabin has air and refills protection.
guide.universe.ship.fly.title: Flying
guide.universe.ship.freighter:
One freighter per player: rescue one in distress or buy one from a ship dealer (from 120,000 credits). Fly into the port-side hangar to go aboard; inside is a big deck to build on.

Bridge console: warp the whole ship for 3 warpers; range C 40, B 45, A 50, S 60 ly
Summon freighter: press N in space and pick it; it arrives 220 blocks ahead, 5 min cooldown

Fall off the deck and you're pulled back to the hangar. Beds set your spawn.
guide.universe.ship.freighter.title: Freighters
guide.universe.ship.rating:
Ships are rated when assembled. Press B while flying, or sneak + right-click a parked helm, for the ship panel.

Class: fighter, hauler, explorer or shuttle, from guns, cargo and warp drives
Grade: C, B, A, S, from Mk.II parts and alloy plating
Specialty bonus: B +10%, A +20%, S +35%
Tech slots: C 3, B 4, A 5, S 6

Ship modules: thrust efficiency, pulse tuning, hyperdrive booster, deflector, hull reinforcement, fire control
guide.universe.ship.rating.title: Rating and Tech
guide.universe.ship.space_sentinels:
Leave a planet at 3 wanted stars, or hit a freighter in distress 8 times, and Sentinel interceptors chase you, jamming your pulse drive. Destroy them, get 1,200 blocks away or reach a station. Wrecks drop Sentinel scrap, sometimes nav data or a ship module.

Emergency broadcast receiver: sold by tech merchants. Use it while flying in space to find a derelict
Credit chips: right-click to cash in, 1,000 each
guide.universe.ship.warp:
Press M for the star map, pick a system and press Warp.

Needs: piloting in space, a warp drive aboard, a space warper in your inventory
Position: 1,200 blocks from the star, 150 from any atmosphere
Charge: 3.5 s, uses 1 warper
Range: 5 ly, +5 per warp drive (+10 for Mk.II), up to 4 drives

Space warpers come from assemblers or station shops.
guide.universe.ship.warp.title: Warping
guide.universe.start.crash:
The crash site is 60 to 110 blocks from spawn and appears the first time the world loads. Chat tells you which way the smoke is.

The chest holds:
Damaged multitool
Probe log and this guide
Copper, iron and redstone
2 oxygen capsules, 2 hazard cells
guide.universe.start.crash.title: The Crash Site
guide.universe.start.laser:
The multitool also carries a mining laser, a scanner and a plasma gun.

Hold right-click: mining laser
Sneak + right-click: scan
G: switch mining and combat mode

Laser: 10 blocks, 1.5x dig speed
Overheat: after 4 s, cools for 2 s
Scan: veins 32, points of interest 200, 5 s cooldown
Plasma bolt: 5 damage

Lasering on planets draws Sentinels.
guide.universe.start.laser.title: Laser and Scanner
guide.universe.start.multitool:
The multitool is your main early tool: pickaxe, shovel and axe in one. Repair the damaged one with copper, redstone and iron; the crash chest has exactly enough.
Without a crash site, craft one from scratch with a diamond.
Either way you get a C-grade pistol.

Mining tier: iron
Dig speed: 6
guide.universe.start.multitool.title: The Multitool
guide.universe.start.suit:
All four pieces use iron and copper. Helmet plus chestplate seals the suit.
Fewer pieces drain faster: x2 with three, x3.5 with two, x6 with one.

Oxygen: 10 min sealed, 15 s unsealed
Hazard protection: 5 min, full set
No drain in the Overworld, stations or ships
guide.universe.start.suit.title: The Exosuit
guide.universe.start.tools:
Multitools come in five classes, graded C to S. Higher grades get more slots and a bigger bonus.

Pistol: mining speed
Rifle: weapon damage
Experimental: scan range
Alien: damage and scan
Sentinel: damage, highest bonus

Slots: C 4, B 5, A 6, S 8
Bonus: C 0, B 10%, A 20%, S 35%
Station cabinets sell 3 a day. Trade in the one you hold; its modules move over.
guide.universe.start.tools.title: Multitool Classes
guide.universe.survival.acid:
The seas of toxic planets are sulfuric acid. Standing in it drains your toxic protection fast and being indoors does not help; once the protection is gone it burns you. Items dropped in it corrode away — glass, gold and plastic do not.

These planets get acid rain. It counts together with toxic air, so find cover before your protection runs out.

A water pump on an acid source pumps sulfuric acid, which gives you acid without a chemical line. A bucket takes one acid with you.

Submarines work in acid. Nothing grows in these seas and there are no fish.
guide.universe.survival.acid.title: Acid Seas and Acid Rain
guide.universe.survival.border: A planet's surface has an edge centered on (0, 0): about 2000 blocks across on small moons, up to 30000 on large planets. Within 64 blocks the suit panel warns you and the screen edges turn red. You can't walk past it; take your ship. The home planet has no edge.
guide.universe.survival.border.title: Planet Edge
guide.universe.survival.cooking:
Burns any furnace fuel, alien logs too. Pick a recipe on the left.

One ingredient: 2.5 s, combined: 5 s
Cactus juice, cactus jelly: +20% oxygen
Custards: +25% all protection
Spicy dishes, root soup: slower cold drain
Stations buy combined dishes
guide.universe.survival.cooking.title: Nutrient Processor
guide.universe.survival.core:
An exosuit carries the mecha's energy core. Flight, faster walking and drones draw on it; life support does not. Press B for the mecha panel.

Core: 120 kJ, more with Mecha Core
Fuel chamber: 800 W, more with Energy Circuit
Put fuel in the chamber; with auto refuel on it takes more of the same from your inventory
Wireless power towers also charge it, up to 15 kW
guide.universe.survival.core.title: Mecha Energy Core
guide.universe.survival.flight:
With Drive Engine you can fly like in creative: double-tap jump. Run out of energy and you drift down without fall damage. This flight does not work in space.

Hover: 1.2 kW, plus 100 W per m/s
Drive Engine 1-4: speed x1, x1.3, x1.6, x2
Mechanical Frame: walking +10% per level for 6 levels, then +20% for 2; only the extra speed costs energy
guide.universe.survival.flight.title: Mecha Flight
guide.universe.survival.hazards:
Two hazards max: cold, heat, toxic, radiation.

Full suit: 5 min, refills 25 s after
Empty: -1 HP/2 s; no oxygen -2 HP/s
Under a roof with walls: no drain, refills in 20 s
Storms x2; fire or ice counters the opposite
Capsules and cells: +50%, auto below 20%
guide.universe.survival.hazards.title: Hazards
guide.universe.survival.hydroponics:
Unlocked by Hydroponics. Connect power (20 kW), use a plant product on it to sow, right-click to harvest, sneak to uproot. Sorters can take the harvest. Works on any planet.

Oxygen: 3 min, sodium: 5 min, others: 10-30 min
4-8 per harvest
guide.universe.survival.modules:
Press U for tech configuration to fit modules and sort cargo.

Exosuit: starts with 4 tech slots and 9 cargo; each repaired drop pod adds 1 slot and 9 cargo, up to 12 and 54
Multitool: 6 tech slots
Grades: C, B, A, S; up to three of one kind count
Sources: assemblers make C, better ones come from points of interest and stations

Jetpack: jump again in mid-air for 2.5 s of thrust, recharges in 2 s on the ground
guide.universe.survival.modules.title: Tech Modules
guide.universe.survival.refiner:
Burns fuel. Keeps its contents when broken.

Rock x4: oxygen
Ice, snow, cactus flesh, water bucket: water
Logs: charcoal; sand: glass; raw ore: ingots
Oxygen x4: capsule; sodium x4: hazard cell
Frost crystal, solanium, gamma root, mould x2: the four gels, +40% to one protection
guide.universe.survival.refiner.title: Portable Refiner
guide.universe.survival.resources:
Patches of harvestable plants grow on planets. Right-click with an empty hand to harvest; they grow back in about 15 minutes.

Oxygen Bladderwort: oxygen, right-click for +10% oxygen
Saltwort, salt crystals: sodium, +8% protection
Each planet type has its own plant; caves have marrow
Plant a product on soil where it grows wild
Picking gravitino balls angers the Sentinels
guide.universe.survival.resources.title: Resource Plants
guide.universe.survival.sentinels:
Laser mining, hunting and attacking Sentinels raise the alert. Fill it and you are wanted.

Five levels. Destroy a wave to go up one:
1: drones
2: a repair drone joins
3+: heavy drones, summoners, quads
5: a walker

Kill repair drones and summoners first. Quads and walkers take double damage from behind. Stay out of sight 20 + 10 × level seconds to escape. Beat level 5 and the Sentinels leave for 10 minutes.
guide.universe.survival.sentinels.title: Sentinels
guide.universe.survival.weapons:
Fit one of each into multitool slots. G cycles mining, blaster and fitted weapons.

Scatter Blaster: 8 pellets, 16 m
Pulse Spitter: 10 shots/s, wide spread, runs hot
Blaze Javelin: hold 1.5 s, release, hits to 120 m
Plasma Launcher: bouncing grenade, 2 s fuse
Shares the laser's heat. Weapon modules add damage and fire rate.
Research: Plasma Weapons, Heavy Plasma Weapons
guide.universe.survival.weapons.title: Multitool Weapons
guide.universe.trade.missions:
Mission boards post 3 missions a day. Hold one at a time and hand it in where you took it.

Delivery: 1.6x the cargo value
Bounty: 220 per pirate
Mining: 70 per asteroid
Survey: 150 per species

Rewards scale with the station's wealth and sometimes include navigation data or a module.
guide.universe.trade.missions.title: Missions
guide.universe.trade.pirates:
Pirates can appear while you pilot in space more than 600 blocks from a station. A roll every 6 to 10 minutes, likelier with valuable cargo. 5 s after the warning, 2 to 4 fighters show up behind you.

Left-click: fire
G: photon cannon / mining beam
Escape: warp, land, reach a station or get 400 blocks away
Reward: a bounty per kill, scrap in your hold

A destroyed ship is towed to the station and each cargo stack loses 30%.
guide.universe.trade.pirates.title: Pirates
guide.universe.trade.stations:
Every system has one space station, 700 blocks outside the first landable planet. Fly in through the hangar and set down on the pad.

Trade terminal: buy and sell
Mission board: take missions
Ship repair console: 2 credits per hull point
Station teleporter: no power needed

Inside there is gravity and air. Outside you float: jump to rise, sneak to sink.
guide.universe.trade.stations.title: Space Stations
guide.universe.trade.trading:
Trade terminals are in space stations. Credits are kept on death.

Sell: click 1, Shift a stack, Ctrl all
Buy: click 1, Shift a stack

Prices drop as you sell the same thing and recover by half every 2 days.
Categories the system lacks: +30%
Local products: -25%

Every station sells warpers, fuel, thrusters and weapons; wealthy ones stock Mk.II parts.
guide.universe.trade.trading.title: Trading

jei.universe.info.alien_fish: Dropped by sea life on planets with seas.
jei.universe.info.creature_egg: Well-fed companions that trust you lay eggs. Placed on a solid block, an egg hatches in 5 minutes into a companion. It carries species, size, color and temperament.
jei.universe.info.critical_photon: A ray receiver in photon mode turns Dyson sphere energy into critical photons, 1.2 GJ each. A graviton lens doubles the power.
jei.universe.info.crude_oil: An oil extractor has to sit on a crude oil seep. Seeps slow down as you pump them, down to a floor.
jei.universe.info.deuterium: A fractionator turns 1% of the hydrogen passing through into deuterium. Hydrogen leaves the front, deuterium the top.
jei.universe.info.egg_sequencer: Edits a creature egg, one trait per material: bio gel makes it bigger, bone meal smaller, dye recolors it, herbivore feed makes it docile, raw meat territorial.
jei.universe.info.exo_mech: A two-legged mech. Steps up 2 blocks; hold jump to fire the jets. The sealed cabin has air and blocks planet hazards. Left-click fires the blaster cannon.
jei.universe.info.fossil: Dug from Fossil Dirt in fossil pits on habitable, barren, scorched and frozen planets. Sell-only.
jei.universe.info.fulgurite: Fused where lightning hits sand, soil or rock in a thunderstorm. Mine it with a pickaxe; sells at space stations.
jei.universe.info.heavy_rover: Slow eight-wheeled hauler with a 54-slot hold. A portable refiner rides on the back: sneak + right-click the rear to open it. It keeps working while you drive.
jei.universe.info.hover_car: The fastest vehicle. Floats a block above the ground and crosses water. 18-slot hold.
jei.universe.info.kelp_pod: Candlelight Kelp grows on the seabed of planets with seas and glows when ripe. Each pod restores 15 oxygen and can be planted back on the seabed.
jei.universe.info.knowledge_stone: Found on every planet you can land on, and in every settlement's plaza. Right-click to learn a word of the system's dominant race, once per stone per player. Can't be mined.
jei.universe.info.living_pearl: Pry open clams on the deep seabeds of planets with seas. Sell-only, and worth a lot.
jei.universe.info.multitool: Multitools come as Pistol, Rifle, Experimental, Alien and Sentinel, graded C to S. A crafted one is an A-Class Pistol. Buy other classes from the cabinet in a station lobby. Trade a Walker Brain at a Sentinel Pillar for a Sentinel one.
jei.universe.info.multitool_cabinet: Found only in station lobbies. Stocks 3 tools a day; richer systems sell better grades. Buy while holding your old multitool to trade it in. Its modules and weapons move to the new one.
jei.universe.info.quadruped_servo: Dropped by sentinel quads. They join the hunt from wanted level 3, and one patrols outside each manufacturing facility. Hits from behind do double damage.
jei.universe.info.salvaged_scrap: Found in salvage capsules, buried under 3 shell plates at salvage sites. Sell-only.
jei.universe.info.tool_weapon: Fit into a multitool tech slot (U). Press G to cycle mining, blaster and fitted weapons. Weapon modules on the tool boost damage and fire rate.
jei.universe.info.vehicle_summoner: Right-click to call one of your deployed vehicles to the front of the pad, even from another dimension. Submarines need water there.
jei.universe.info.walker_brain: Dropped by sentinel walkers, which only come at wanted level 5. They turn slowly: get behind them and hit the vent for double damage. Right-click a Sentinel Pillar terminal with it to get a Sentinel multitool.
jei.universe.info.water: A water pump on top of a water source block pumps 50 water a minute. Acid seas don't count.

poi.universe.log.ending.1: We leave for the landing site at dawn. I'm leaving the terminal on. Maybe the next person can use it.
poi.universe.log.ending.2: If you're reading this, take whatever is in the crates. We won't need it anymore.
poi.universe.log.ending.3: End of entry. Power at four percent.
poi.universe.log.ending.4: I've left a copy of our navigation data on this terminal. Head toward the signal.
poi.universe.log.ending.5: More tomorrow. The aurora tonight is beautiful. We all went out to watch.
poi.universe.log.ending.6: (The rest of this entry is corrupted and cannot be read.)
poi.universe.log.event.1: Three Sentinels came this afternoon. They just watched the mining rig for a while, then left.
poi.universe.log.event.2: %1$s went out to check the pipeline and hasn't come back. The beacon shows the signal stopped in the eastern valley, not moving.
poi.universe.log.event.3: A meteor came down nearby and the shockwave shattered two windows. We saved the impact coordinates to the navigation data.
poi.universe.log.event.4: Someone went through the supply crates in storage, but the lock is untouched. %1$s says we must have miscounted.
poi.universe.log.event.5: The reactor readings have started to jump. We shut down half the equipment and keep a single light on at night.
poi.universe.log.event.6: The signal booster caught a repeating transmission, not on any of our frequencies. %1$s recorded it.
poi.universe.log.event.7: Another section of ground collapsed, opening a deep shaft. %1$s dropped a glowstick in. We never heard it land.
poi.universe.log.event.8: The company finally answered: outpost decommissioned, personnel to evacuate on their own. It didn't say how.
poi.universe.log.opening.1: Outpost %1$s, day %2$s of deployment. Log entry by %3$s.
poi.universe.log.opening.3: Automatic logging restored. Outpost %1$s, day %2$s, on duty: %3$s.
poi.universe.log.opening.4: Day %2$s. Outpost %1$s. This is %3$s. If anyone finds this recording—
poi.universe.log.situation.1: The supply ship is late again. %1$s locked the last crate of oxygen capsules away and says we ration from today.
poi.universe.log.situation.2: The drill rig died in last night's storm. %1$s worked on it all night and still couldn't get it turning.
poi.universe.log.situation.3: The ore here is richer than the survey promised. %1$s says one more season and we can all retire.
poi.universe.log.situation.4: %1$s insists there is knocking under the floor at night. I listened. Nothing.
poi.universe.log.situation.5: The comm array only picks up static. %1$s has realigned the antenna thirty times; the signal hasn't changed.
poi.universe.log.situation.6: The temperature swings get worse every day and our suit protection won't hold for long. %1$s has started coughing.
poi.universe.log.situation.7: We found a stone covered in symbols on the northern ridge. %1$s took pictures and says it can't be natural.
poi.universe.log.situation.8: Found a new creature today. %1$s gave it an awful name and logged it in the discovery log anyway.
poi.universe.lore.1.text: Traveler, you can hear us. Long ago we too set out from one small world, looked up at the sky, and believed the stars would never go dark.
poi.universe.lore.1.title: Echo
poi.universe.lore.10.text: At the heart of the cluster is something that swallows light. Our last fleet flew toward it. Some called it escape. Some called it going home.
poi.universe.lore.10.title: The Center
poi.universe.lore.11.text: You will build your rings and your shells too. We will not stop you; we cannot. We only want you to know what they cost.
poi.universe.lore.11.title: Choice
poi.universe.lore.12.text: If one day your sky begins to dim, remember to come back here and lay your hand on the stone. We will hear you.
poi.universe.lore.12.title: Last Words
poi.universe.lore.2.text: We learned to tame stars. The day the first ring closed around our sun, our nights were never dark again. We had more energy than we could ever use, so we went looking for more stars.
poi.universe.lore.2.title: The First Ring
poi.universe.lore.3.text: A thousand stars wrapped in our shells. Light flowed along the roads we laid, from one system to the next. We called it prosperity.
poi.universe.lore.3.title: The Web of Stars
poi.universe.lore.4.text: We hollowed out world after world. Forests became pits, oceans became coolant pools. Planets do not protest, so we heard nothing.
poi.universe.lore.4.title: Quiet Worlds
poi.universe.lore.5.text: Later we built the Sentinels to watch over the worlds that remained. They know no masters, only harm. The ones you meet today are their descendants.
poi.universe.lore.5.title: Sentinels
poi.universe.lore.6.text: We quarreled over the stars. Some wanted the shells torn down so starlight could reach the barren worlds again. Others said we still did not have nearly enough.
poi.universe.lore.6.title: Fracture
poi.universe.lore.7.text: The farthest systems began to dim, one after another. They were not dying; they were being enclosed. Someone among us was building in secret, and we never learned who.
poi.universe.lore.7.title: Dimming
poi.universe.lore.8.text: Then came the Silence. Every channel went quiet at once, as if someone had closed a door. We never understood what lay on the other side.
poi.universe.lore.8.title: The Silence
poi.universe.lore.9.text: Those who remained raised these monoliths. We carved our memories into stone, because stone outlives us. Part of the survey data in your hands came from us.
poi.universe.lore.9.title: Monoliths
poi.universe.response.1.text: You came back. Your star has dimmed a little; we felt it. We said we would hear you, and we have been listening all this time.
poi.universe.response.1.title: You Came Back
poi.universe.response.2.text: We enclosed too many stars. The light of the cluster began to flow toward one place, the center. It swallowed every channel. That was the Silence.
poi.universe.response.2.title: Where the Silence Came From
poi.universe.response.3.text: The center feeds on the energy we gathered. The more we gathered, the faster it grew. Half the systems that went dark were eaten by it.
poi.universe.response.3.title: The Center
poi.universe.response.4.text: Our last fleet flew in carrying every joule we had stored, to give it back. The fleet never returned, but from that day on the center stopped growing.
poi.universe.response.4.title: The Fleet
poi.universe.response.5.text: You call it the universe matrix. We called it the key. It weaves matter, energy and information together in a form the center can read. With it, energy can be taken, and it can be returned.
poi.universe.response.5.title: The Key
poi.universe.response.6.text: Finish your research. Then you will see that the shells were only a beginning. When you gather, remember to keep a share to give back.
poi.universe.response.6.title: A Last Request
story.universe.ending.2: The Universe Survey had two goals: map this cluster, and find a source of energy a civilization could live on indefinitely.
story.universe.ending.3: You did both. Every system you crossed and every species you named is in my records. You lit a star of your own and wrapped another in shells.
story.universe.ending.4: The Precursors walked this road before you. They enclosed a thousand stars, and then the Silence came. It only stopped when their last fleet gave the energy back to the center.
story.universe.ending.5: The universe matrix in your hands is the key they spoke of. The center can read us now.
story.universe.ending.6: How much you take from here, and how much you give back, is up to you. The monoliths will still be there.
story.universe.ending.7: I never heard from the other eleven probes again. I will keep sending my own signal until the battery runs out.
story.universe.ending.8: If someone finds me on some planet one day, tell them someone made it to the end.
story.universe.ending.skip: Hold Space to speed up, Esc to close
story.universe.ending.title: UNV-7 · Final Log
story.universe.log.first_shell: The first shell panel is complete. From here that star looks a little dimmer. The monoliths said it: when your sky begins to dim, go back and lay your hand on the stone.
story.universe.log.first_shell.title: UNV-7 · Shell
story.universe.log.first_space: You're out of the atmosphere and the signal is much clearer. The survey launched twelve probes. I'm the only one still transmitting.
story.universe.log.first_space.title: UNV-7 · Orbit
story.universe.log.first_universe_matrix: The first universe matrix is done. Its readings sit on the same frequency as the signal in the monoliths. I checked three times.
story.universe.log.first_warp: During the jump I lost your signal for four seconds. The other probes all sent their last position report right after a jump.
story.universe.log.first_warp.title: UNV-7 · Jump
